messages:
oliver: Heads up — after the 03/17 runtime rollout I'm seeing slow but steady heap growth on pool-5 hosts for long chat sessions. p95 KV residency is up ~+18pp and eviction_count tick rate doubled. Not a hard outage but memory climbs over 30m sessions. Anyone else?

maria: saw the same on canary. I traced a few traces and KV page reuse looks poor for long contexts — lots of small fragments stuck around.

jake: did we change batching heuristics in that rollout? small batches can increase KV churn if prefix reuse differs.

oliver: yep batching tweak and a kernel-selection fallback landed (PR #4128). suspicious that fallback leaves pages partially populated. attaching a short pprof diff (top lines):

oliver: ```
(pprof) top10
220.27MB  220.27MB  runtime.mallocgc
90.01MB   90.01MB   github.com/redwood/kv.(*page).allocFrag
45.50MB   45.50MB   github.com/redwood/kv.(*cache).insert
20.12MB   20.12MB   github.com/redwood/runtime/serving.handleRequest
```

anya: interesting. Can you post the metric snippets (Prom) for residency + evictions + page_count? want to see per-session split.

oliver: here's what I pulled quickly from prod metrics (PromQL):

oliver: ```promql
# percent of active pages resident per session (0-1)
sum(kv_page_resident{env="prod"}) by (session_id) / sum(kv_page_total{env="prod"}) by (session_id)

# eviction rate per host
rate(kv_evictions_total{host=~"pool-5.*"}[5m])

# page fragmentation estimate (approx): pages with reused_slots < 0.4
sum(kv_page_reused_slots_ratio{env="prod"} < 0.4) by (host)
```

kevin: For dashboarding we should avoid session cardinality explosion — do aggregates and percentiles: e.g., `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(kv_residency_bucket[5m])) by (le))` and a panel split by route for top N routes.

maria: +1. Also propose these new meters: `kv_eviction_by_age_bucket`, `kv_residency_pctile_by_route`, `kv_frag_ratio_avg` and `kv_compaction_runs`. That gives us signal for long-lived sessions vs short chats.

jake: Sample alert suggestions:
- High residency tail: p95(kv_residency_pct_by_host) > 0.6 for 10m -> run compaction job + notify runtime oncall
- Eviction spike: rate(kv_evictions_total[5m]) > 100/s across pool-5 -> rollback candidate
- Frag growth: kv_frag_ratio_avg increases > 20% week-over-week -> schedule offline compaction

oliver: Also we should record a lightweight per-request tag for `context_length_bucket` (short/medium/long) so we can attribute residency and reuse to context length without exploding labels.

anya: Good call. If we add that tag we can make a dashboard: rows = context_length_bucket, panels = residency p50/p95, eviction rate, reuse_ratio, active_pages.

deploy-bot: canary deploy 2026-03-17T03:12:01Z -> pool-5 (deployment id de-7619)

sre-bot: incident alert muted (auto) — low severity mem drift ongoing on pool-5, see thread.

kevin: I'll wire up the PromQL as provisional panels in the runtime Grafana. Will also add a small job to emit `kv_residency_pct_by_route` as a derived metric (1m scrape).

maria: I'll take the pprof diff and try a local repro with long-context generator. If fragmentation shows, I'll triage compaction strategies (lazy / background / opportunistic).

oliver: plan: (1) temporary alert for p95 residency on pool-5, (2) add context_length_bucket tag, (3) add frag_ratio and eviction_by_age metrics, (4) investigate compaction strategies. Assigning tasks: kevin -> dashboard + alert; maria -> repro & compaction experiment; jake -> audit PR #4128 kernel fallback for partial-page behavior.

anya: sounds good. small follow-up: can we add `kv_eviction_age_bucket` labels (0-10s,10-60s,1-10m,10m+) so we know if evictions are evicting very recent entries vs old ones?

oliver: yes please. that will help tell churn vs steady trimming.

kevin: created a draft dashboard here: https://grafana.internal/r/9K2xJk/kv-residency-sessions (will update with derived metric soon).

maria: taking notes in the perf board: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/RUN-2123-kv-frag-repro

oliver: thanks — will keep thread updated. if it gets worse we rollback the batching tweak. :thumbsup:
